label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
Tolu, I’m in Biology 100L now, and Medicine was my first choice too. I scored 251 in JAMB, applied for Medicine and Surgery, and got offered Biology at a federal university here in Lagos. So I know that portal shock. When I saw Biology, I locked myself in my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t even eat. My mum kept telling people in church I was studying Medicine for about two months; I had to beg her to stop. I’m not saying all that to make you feel worse—just to say your reaction is understandable.

On transfer, what our level adviser told us is that you need at least a 4.5 CGPA out of 5.0, and there has to be space in Medicine. She said about six people transferred in from the whole faculty last year, and she thinks more than 40 applied. She also said you need to meet the Medicine cut-offs for JAMB and post-UTME. I don’t know your school’s cut-offs or your post-UTME score, so your 268 by itself doesn’t tell us whether you’re eligible.

For my own situation, my CGPA after first semester is 4.31—not 4.5—so I’m still trying. Transfer is real, but it’s competitive and not something I’d advise anyone to count on as automatic. Kingsley saying it’s a myth isn’t right, but “just read hard” makes it sound much simpler than it is. Please go to your faculty or department and ask for the exact transfer rules at your school, including the cut-offs, application process and timing. Don’t rely just on forum replies, mine included.

Biology itself isn’t a bad course. I was so focused on Medicine that I didn’t expect to enjoy it, but I’m liking genetics and cell biology more than I thought I would. In 100L we take BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST courses. Physics and maths are the ones giving people the most trouble in my set, so be ready to put in work there. There are also practical costs to plan for: my lab coat was ₦6,500, my dissecting kit was ₦9,000, and the practical manual was extra. At our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted; I was fine. Weirdly, that was when I realised I actually liked this kind of work.

I also want to be honest about rewriting. My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected a Pharmacy offer to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and is still at home. That doesn’t mean rewriting is wrong, or that the same thing will happen to you. Staying home for another year can be harder than people make it sound, but if you’re prepared for that possibility and you still want to try again, rewriting is a valid choice. Just don’t accept Biology on the assumption that transfer is guaranteed.

Maybe ask yourself, as honestly as you can: do you want to study Medicine, or do you mainly feel you have to become a doctor for your parents or because that was the plan? Neither answer is something to be ashamed of, but it may help you decide what risk you’re willing to take.

You don’t have to decide based on pressure from your dad, aunty or strangers online. Get the official rules from your school, think through both options, and choose with your eyes open. Whichever way you go, this isn’t the end of the world. Biology can be a good course, and wanting to try again for Medicine is okay too.
